standard.title: Discover possibilities and develop ideas
standard.description: use play, imagination, arts knowledge, processes and/or skills to discover possibilities and develop ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: Students bring informal play experience with materials and imaginative scenarios. No formal arts processes or skills assumed.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use play, imagination and emerging arts knowledge to discover possibilities and develop ideas for artworks.

nodes.label: Noticing and describing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can notice and describe visual or tactile qualities in materials and their environment — naming what they observe (rough, smooth, round, jagged; colours, shapes, lines).
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least two qualities of a material or environment feature observed.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and describe shapes, colours, lines and textures in materials and the environment; make connections between observed qualities and possible uses in artworks.
wider: Explore how natural and human-made materials feel and look differently — collect, sort and name qualities across a range of materials
Use a digital camera or device to capture lines, shapes and colours found in the school environment — describe what you found
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot name or attend to visual and tactile qualities cannot use them purposefully in developing ideas — the observational foundation for all subsequent making is missing.

response_modes.reason: Students need a vocabulary of qualities they can notice and name. Repeated exposure across many materials builds the observational repertoire that fuels idea development.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of qualities available to notice (tactile, visual, environmental) and the range of materials to notice them in is genuinely broad — students who explore many material contexts develop richer noticing.
success_criteria: Names at least two visual or tactile qualities of a material or environmental feature
Makes a connection between a quality and how it might be used in an artwork or creative activity

nodes.label: Playing and experimenting
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use play, trial and imagination to discover new possibilities with materials, movement or voice — noticing what happens when they try something and building on it.
nodes.minimum_width: Try at least two ways of using a material or process; describe what was discovered.
nodes.typical_width: Use play, games and imagination to experiment with materials, movement and voice across multiple forms; identify what worked, what surprised and what could be used in future artworks.
wider: Respond to music by making visual marks — use crayons, paint or other media to express what the music makes you feel or see
Improvise movements or vocalisation to represent a tactile quality (rough, smooth, bouncy) — then translate the same idea into a visual form

response_modes.reason: Play-based discovery depends on variety of stimulus. Students who only experiment in one medium or context develop narrow ideas. More material and sensory contexts produce richer possibilities.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Cross-arts experimentation (visual response to music, translating movement into image) is particularly rich at Foundation — these connections are natural at this age and build lasting creative habits.
success_criteria: Tries at least two different ways of using a material or process
Describes at least one discovery — something that surprised them or that they want to use again

nodes.label: Developing ideas from play
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use something discovered through play or imagination as the starting point for developing an idea for an artwork.
nodes.minimum_width: Take one discovery from play or experimentation and use it as the starting point for an artwork idea.
nodes.typical_width: Use play, experimentation and emerging arts knowledge across multiple forms to develop ideas for artworks; ask 'what if?' questions to push ideas further; document discoveries informally.
wider: Explore how First Nations Australians connect visual arts, story and place — use resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians to see how ideas are developed into artworks
Use a camera to capture the steps in a play-based discovery as a photographic story — share the story and explain the idea it developed

response_modes.reason: This node connects noticing and experimenting into the idea-development process. Students bring together what they have observed, tried and imagined to generate an artwork idea.

success_criteria: Uses a discovery from play or experimentation as the basis for an artwork idea
Can explain what they want to make and what gave them the idea
